findings.issue_text: [BUG] `organization_context` is not defined anywhere in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get, so the expression `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises NameError on every request to this endpoint. Every GET of /api/0/organizations/<slug>/audit-logs/ returns a 500 NameError, fully breaking audit log listing, because the authorization expression is evaluated unconditionally (before the optimized_pagination query param is checked).

[BUG] Django QuerySet slicing with a negative start raises ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported"), so `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with `start_offset = cursor.offset < 0` crashes instead of "properly handling negative slicing automatically" as the comment claims. Any request with a negative cursor offset through the OptimizedCursorPaginator path raises ValueError and returns a 500; the claimed 'advanced feature' is mechanically impossible against the Django ORM.

[BUG] `DateTimePaginator`-style key handling via `self.key`/`self._is_asc` is inherited from BasePaginator, but OptimizedCursorPaginator defaults `cursor = Cursor(0, 0, 0)` and `cursor_value = 0`, so build_queryset filters against value 0 on first page, which for a datetime-typed key ('-datetime') compares datetime field to integer 0 and yields wrong/empty results rather than the first page. First-page requests (no cursor) under optimized mode produce empty or type-error results for datetime-keyed ordering, since the paginator hardcodes cursor_value 0 instead of skipping the filter.

[ADVISORY] `paginate()` may not forward an `enable_advanced_features` kwarg to the paginator class; the endpoint's OrganizationEndpoint.paginate signature accepts specific kwargs (paginator_cls, order_by, on_results, etc.) and unknown kwargs either raise TypeError or are silently dropped, making the flag a silent no-op. If silently dropped, OptimizedCursorPaginator runs with enable_advanced_features=False so the advertised optimization path never activates and operators cannot tell; if TypeError, the optimized branch 500s. Either way the feature gate does not do what the code says.

[BUG] The optimized-pagination gate reads `organization_context.member.has_global_access`, but `organization_context` is never defined in this function or module. Every audit-log GET request that has `optimized_pagination=true` raises NameError before any queryset work, returning a 500 instead of the paginated rows — the 'enhanced' path has no working access check at all and can never be reached.

[BUG] The 'advanced' branch slices the queryset with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]` where start_offset < 0), which Django ORM querysets do not support. Any request carrying a cursor with a negative offset through OptimizedCursorPaginator (the exact case this branch exists for) raises `ValueError: Negative indices are not supported` and 500s — the advertised negative-offset feature crashes on its first and only trigger, and the comment 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false.

[BUG] The shared get_result change removes the implicit floor on offset for prev cursors, so the default (non-optimized) path now slices with a raw possibly-negative offset when `cursor.is_prev` is true. All existing endpoints using this paginator can crash with Django's negative-slice ValueError once a cursor with negative offset (now constructible per the cursors.py change) arrives, and even with non-negative cursors this silently alters slicing for every prev-page request with no verification in the diff.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls `self._is_asc(for_prev)`, but `_is_asc` is defined on OffsetPaginator, not on BasePaginator. Any pagination flow that reaches get_item_key through this paginator (including the prev-cursor dedup path in its own get_result) raises AttributeError and 500s.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a new behavior-bearing paginator class, a query-param-gated code path in the audit-log endpoint, and a behavior change to the shared get_result, yet contains no test-shaped files at all (no spec/test files anywhere in the diff). The negative-slice crash, the NameError in the gate, and the default-path slicing change are all unverified; the next contributor changing cursor semantics has no spec to pin expected slicing behavior, and regressions in the shared get_result affect every paginated endpoint with zero coverage.

[ADVISORY] The only gating flags enumerated are `optimized_pagination` and superuser/global-access; the authorization gate is checked against `request.user` directly while the endpoint has an `organization` object in scope, and there is no flag-equivalent for org-scoped admin roles (e.g. org owner/manager with global access on other orgs). Org-level owners who legitimately administer this organization but lack is_superuser/global bit silently fall back to the slow paginator — the feature ships inert for the primary admin population, and nothing in the diff verifies which member tiers actually reach the optimized path.

[ADVISORY] The negative-offset 'advanced' branch contains no acceptance criterion for what results negative offsets should return; the Cursor default in get_result (`Cursor(0,0,0)`) and the build_cursor signature are unchanged, so no code path in this diff ever produces a negative-offset cursor. The entire feature is dead code: no producer of negative offsets exists in the diff, so operators cannot trigger it and its behavior (which crashes when triggered) is unverifiable — the simplest fix is deleting the branch and the enable_advanced_features plumbing.

[BUG] The shared BasePaginator.get_result now slices the queryset with a negative start offset (start_offset = cursor.offset when cursor.is_prev), which Django's QuerySet slicing explicitly rejects: `Negative indexing is not supported` (QuerySet.__setitem__/slice raises ValueError/AssertionError on negative bounds). Any prev-cursor carrying a negative offset sent to ANY endpoint using this base paginator raises an unhandled exception and returns a 500, a global regression introduced for a change scoped to one audit-log endpoint.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result's 'advanced' path executes queryset[cursor.offset:...] with cursor.offset < 0, and Django ORM queryset slicing raises on negative bounds, so the advertised negative-offset feature crashes on first use. A superuser requesting ?optimized_pagination=true with a crafted negative-offset cursor gets a 500 instead of the 'efficient reverse pagination' the feature promises; the feature can never have worked.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor(value))/math.ceil(value) on the item's key, but the audit-log endpoint orders by datetime, so floor()/ceil() are called on a datetime and then int() on a datetime raises TypeError ('int() argument must be ... not datetime.datetime'). The first serialized row of an optimized-paginated audit-log response crashes with a TypeError/500 for the exact endpoint this paginator was built for — the paginator was copied from a float-keyed implementation and is incompatible with its only call site.

[BUG] When cursor.value is falsy, cursor_value defaults to 0, and this 0 is passed to build_queryset, which for a datetime-keyed queryset becomes queryset.filter(datetime__lt=0) (or gt), returning no rows instead of the first page. The first page of optimized audit-log pagination returns an empty result set for every request without a cursor, so the feature silently returns zero rows.

[BUG] The gate reads organization_context.member.has_global_access, but the endpoint (OrganizationAuditPermission on control silo) only guarantees request.access; organization_context.member is not defined in this view's flow and the audit-log queryset is scoped by organization, so either the attribute raises AttributeError (500) or it bypasses organization-scoping semantics without any requirement authorizing it. Non-superuser admins hitting this code path get a 500 (AttributeError) or, if the attribute resolves, the pagination variant is granted based on an access level never stated in the PR intent — an undocumented permission expansion.

[ADVISORY] The optimized path is gated on a raw query parameter `optimized_pagination=true` combined with superuser/global-access, with no feature-flag, options entry, or API surface documentation — behavior changes for privileged clients purely from a query string not traceable to any stated requirement. Operators cannot disable or roll out the new pagination path without a code deploy, and the PR intent ('performance for high-volume audit logs') does not mention an admin-only gated query-param variant; reviewers and clients cannot discover the contract.

[ADVISORY] Scope drift: modifying shared BasePaginator.get_result (used by every paginator in the codebase) is not traceable to the audit-log pagination requirement; the change alters slicing semantics for all endpoints to accommodate a hypothetical negative-offset feature that no existing cursor producer generates. The next paginator regression anywhere in Sentry has a new (never-exercised) branch to bisect through, and the diff's stated intent (one endpoint's performance) now carries risk across the whole API surface.

[ADVISORY] Scope drift/under-scoping: the entire OptimizedCursorPaginator class (including enable_advanced_features, negative-offset traversal, 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds') is implementation work not traceable to the stated intent of faster pagination of audit logs; cursor pagination by definition needs no offset math at all, so the class adds an attack-shaped capability (bypassing pagination bounds) unrelated to any requirement. A privileged or forged client can request offsets that step outside the normal pagination window ('access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' per the code's own comment), and the class must be maintained forever for a requirement that could be met by a plain cursor paginator.

[ADVISORY] Duplicated slicing logic: the negative/boundary-offset branch is hand-copied between BasePaginator.get_result (lines 181-186) and OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (855-862), and the two copies have already drifted (one clamps via max(0, offset) on is_prev, the other doesn't). A future fix to one copy (e.g., clamping negative offsets) silently misses the other, and the drift already present means the two paginators produce different results for the same cursor, biting whoever debugs pagination next.

[ADVISORY] The post_query_filter is applied to cursor.results but the prev-cursor trimming block above (lines 879-884) compares len(results) == offset + limit + extra against the unfiltered list, mixing pre- and post-filter lengths the base implementation keeps distinct; more broadly this class re-implements get_result wholesale with subtly different invariants (e.g., missing the `elif` handling parity and hits accounting) for no requirement-driven reason. Whoever modifies the shared get_result (e.g., a cursor-dedup or max-hits fix) must remember this near-duplicate or the admin-only audit path diverges in behavior, raising the cost and risk of the next pagination change.

[ADVISORY] The Cursor change adds only a comment claiming negative offsets are now supported, but no code enforces, validates, or uses the claim anywhere — a docs-only mutation of a core utility with no behavior, not traceable to any requirement. The misleading comment tells the next reader that negative offsets are a supported cursor feature, inviting reliance on a behavior that actually crashes (see the paginator findings), so a future change gets built on a false invariant.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a negative start bound (queryset[start_offset:stop] where start_offset is cursor.offset < 0), which Django's ORM does not 'handle automatically' — it raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported...'), so the request 500s. Any admin client that sends a cursor with a negative offset (the exact input this paginator's own docstring advertises as a supported 'advanced' feature) hits a ValueError at query execution and gets a 500 instead of a page of results; the comment 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is factually false.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), but the endpoint instantiates it against a datetime-ordered audit-log queryset (order_by='-datetime'), so the value is a datetime and math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError: an number is required. Every optimized-pagination request over audit logs (whose rows all have datetime keys) crashes with TypeError in get_item_key as soon as build_cursor/get_item_key runs on any result — the 'optimized' path can never return a successful page; a naive int()/float() coercion of a datetime only produces a garbage year number, silently corrupting cursor values even if it didn't raise.

[BUG] The modified BasePaginator.get_result uses `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, so a prev-cursor with a negative offset still produces a negative slice queryset[offset:stop] in the *default* (non-optimized) path, which Django raises ValueError on — the negative-offset path this diff introduces is not actually clamped for the is_prev branch. The defensive clamp only covers the non-prev branch; a prev cursor carrying a negative offset (Cursor.offset is an unvalidated int from the request) crashes the pre-existing DateTimePaginator path with a ValueError 500 where the old code's stop computation at least kept the bound relationship consistent.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator's prev-page post-filter compares `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` using the raw `offset` while the slice was computed from `start_offset`, so when a negative offset is in play the sentinel-length check compares against the wrong bound and the last row is either not dropped or wrongly dropped. A client paginating backwards with the advertised negative-offset mode receives a duplicated or missing boundary row on each prev page, silently corrupting the audit-log traversal that pagination correctness (no missed/duplicated rows) exists to guarantee.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result (a parallel hand-maintained implementation of the same pagination contract) that will drift from the base as BasePaginator evolves. Every future fix to BasePaginator's slicing/cursor logic must be re-applied by hand here or the two paginators silently disagree; this diff itself already demonstrates the drift (the offset vs start_offset divergence above). Deleting the copied body and parameterizing the one behavioral delta (offset clamping) in BasePaginator removes ~70 lines and a whole second code path.

[ADVISORY] New endpoint behavior is gated on the raw query-string parameter `optimized_pagination == "true"` plus an inline permission check (`request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`), with no feature flag/options entry and no shared permission abstraction — a parallel authorization path duplicating the endpoint's existing permission model. Operations cannot disable the crashing optimized path without a code deploy (no flag), and the duplicated ad-hoc permission check drifts from OrganizationAuditPermission; additionally organization_context.member is None for a superuser who is not an org member, so that line raises AttributeError for exactly the user class the check exists to serve.

[ADVISORY] The 'performance optimization' changes nothing about the query shape: the optimized branch runs the same queryset, same order_by, same count/hit logic, and the same O(offset+limit) slice as DateTimePaginator — negative offsets are the only behavioral delta, and those crash rather than accelerate. Reviewers and future maintainers get a misleading signal that the audit-log hot path was optimized when the new code path adds a second, less-tested route with zero performance benefit; the branch should be deleted rather than kept as a divergent path.

[BUG] Allowing negative offsets in queryset slicing crashes with Django's 'AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported when using slice' when a prev-cursor with negative offset hits the modified DateTimePaginator path. Any client sending a crafted cursor with a negative offset to an endpoint using this paginator gets a 500 instead of results; the comment claims the queryset handles negative slicing, but Django ORM explicitly forbids it.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with cursor.offset when it is negative, raising Django's negative-slice AssertionError and returning a 500. The 'advanced feature' path is unusable: whenever enable_advanced_features is on and a negative-offset cursor arrives (the exact scenario the class advertises), list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) raises instead of paginating.

[BUG] get_item_key calls int(math.floor(value))/math.ceil(value) on the cursor key value, which is a datetime for this paginator's -datetime ordering, raising TypeError. Every paginated request through OptimizedCursorPaginator (the auditlogs endpoint orders by -datetime) crashes with a 500 because datetime objects cannot be floored/int-cast; the paginator is copied from the integer-keyed OffsetPaginator without adapting the key type.

[BUG] organization_context.member.has_global_access dereferences member without a None check, raising AttributeError for requests where the user has no organization membership. A superuser (or any authenticated request) hitting the audit logs endpoint for an organization they don't belong to gets a 500 before reaching the paginator, where prior code worked; this line executes on every request, not just the optimized path.

[ADVISORY] The optimized path is gated on an undocumented raw query param 'optimized_pagination' with no feature flag or options entry, so its behavior change (different paginator, different cursor wire format, negative-offset acceptance) cannot be disabled or enabled via configuration. Operators cannot turn the new pagination semantics off without a code deploy, and clients that toggle the param get a silently different response/cursor shape — a rolling-deploy and API-contract risk.

[ADVISORY] The negative-offset branch of OptimizedCursorPaginator is dead-weight copy-paste of the base class get_result (including the redundant max(0, offset) clamping just added above), drifting from the parent implementation and adding places-to-update for future paginator fixes. The next bug fix to BasePaginator.get_result slicing/boundary logic (e.g., the prev-cursor trimming below) will not propagate to this duplicated copy, silently diverging audit-log pagination behavior from every other endpoint.

[ADVISORY] The only test-visible difference between the two branches is the paginator class; the diff adds no tests exercising OptimizedCursorPaginator or the negative-offset path, and a plain smoke request with optimized_pagination=true would have caught the datetime TypeError immediately. The new code path ships untested and non-functional; any audit-log admin UI or script that adopts the param regresses audit-log access.

[BUG] get_result now passes cursor.offset through unclamped whenever cursor.is_prev is true, so a client-crafted cursor with a negative offset reaches queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django's QuerySet slicing rejects negative offsets with ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), so a user-supplied prev cursor with a negative offset turns the endpoint into a 500 instead of the 4xx/valid page the API contract promises; the max(0, offset) clamp that previously prevented this was only applied on the is_prev=False branch.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result executes queryset[cursor.offset:stop] with a client-supplied negative cursor.offset whenever enable_advanced_features is set, relying on a comment claiming 'Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' which is false. The slice raises ValueError, producing a 500 error on the audit-log endpoint for the superuser/global-access population, and the 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' code path is reachable purely from a query-string cursor with no server-side validation of offset bounds.

[ADVISORY] The new OptimizedCursorPaginator path is gated on a raw query parameter (optimized_pagination=true) combined with superuser/global-access status, with no feature flag or options entry. Operators cannot disable or roll out the new paginator behavior without a code deploy, and the divergence between the two paginator implementations (the endpoint's copy of slicing logic vs. the base class) means a bugfix applied to one silently misses the other; also enable_advanced is computed before use, and the superuser check reads organization_context.member without a None guard for users hitting the endpoint outside org-member flow.

[ADVISORY] The prev-cursor dedup branch compares len(results) == offset + limit + extra using the raw client-controlled cursor.offset instead of the clamped start_offset used for slicing. When a negative-offset cursor reaches this branch, the length comparison is computed against a different origin than the slice was, so the off-by-one dedup logic drops or keeps the wrong element — users receive duplicated or missing rows at page boundaries under the optimized path.

[BUG] The negative-offset branch in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result passes a negative start to queryset slicing, which Django ORM does not support and raises AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported."). Any request using optimized_pagination=true with a cursor carrying a negative offset returns a 500 AssertionError instead of the paginated rows the new code promises, and since a client controls the cursor string (offset is parsed from the request cursor), any authorized admin can trigger the crash at will.

[BUG] The modified BasePaginator.get_result sets start_offset = offset (unclamped) whenever cursor.is_prev, so a crafted prev-cursor with a negative offset now reaches queryset[offset:stop] with a negative index on the shared DateTimePaginator path. This diff silently changes behavior of every existing DateTimePaginator endpoint (not just audit logs): a hand-forged prev cursor with negative offset now crashes with Django's 'Negative indexing is not supported' AssertionError instead of being clamped to 0 as before — a client-controlled 500 on previously-safe endpoints.

[ADVISORY] The new OptimizedCursorPaginator path is gated on a raw query parameter optimized_pagination with no feature flag, options entry, or way to disable it short of a code deploy. Operators cannot turn off the new code path when it misbehaves (e.g., the negative-offset crash above) without shipping a revert; the query-param gate also means new clients and old servers coexist unpredictably during rolling deploys.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result accepts cursor.offset verbatim from the client-supplied cursor with no lower bound, coupling the entire advanced path to unvalidated negative integers. The comment 'This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' is unexamined: the queryset bounds row access, but the offset is trusted to shape slicing and cursor arithmetic (build_cursor receives results trimmed by an offset-derived len comparison), enabling the crash in the negative branch and cursor-corruption for arbitrary values.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator's __init__ stores enable_advanced_features, but the 'advanced features' its docstring advertises (bidirectional negative-offset pagination, optimized query path, streamlined boundary handling) consist of a slicing change that is not measurably a query optimization. The class is speculative generality: it duplicates ~70 lines of BasePaginator.get_result with one divergent branch that will drift from the base implementation on every upstream fix (the base get_result at lines 182-186 already diverges from it today), making the next paginator bugfix a two-site change with no test coverage to catch the drift.

[BUG] The modified DateTimePaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a negative start offset when cursor.is_prev is set, e.g. queryset[-5:7], which Django explicitly forbids ("Negative indexing is not supported"), raising an AssertionError. Any client sending a crafted prev-cursor whose decoded offset is negative (Cursor.offset is taken verbatim from the user-supplied cursor) gets a 500 from every endpoint using this paginator instead of the paginated 200 the contract promises.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result passes a negative start offset into queryset[start_offset:stop] under enable_advanced_features, and Django querysets raise "Negative indexing is not supported" rather than "handling boundary conditions automatically" as the comment claims. A superuser or global-access admin hitting /api/0/organizations/<org>/audit-logs/?optimized_pagination=true with a negative-offset cursor gets a 500, and the new paginator is unusable for the reverse pagination it was built for.

[ADVISORY] The new optimized pagination path is gated on the raw query parameter optimized_pagination=true with no feature flag, options entry, or way to disable it short of a code deploy. Operators who need to turn off the buggy negative-offset path during an incident (500s for admin users) cannot do so without a rollback/deploy, and the API surface silently grows an undocumented parameter.

[ADVISORY] The comment "This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level" asserts safety of negative offsets, but negative offsets on the shared Cursor class (utils/cursors.py change) are now accepted without validation, so every paginator that decodes a user cursor can receive a negative offset. The next paginator or endpoint change that trusts offset>=0 (e.g. arithmetic like offset - limit for prev-cursor building in build_cursor) silently produces wrong cursors or wrong pages for forged cursors, and the misleading comment hides that the validation was deliberately dropped in this diff.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a negative start index when the client supplies a cursor with negative offset, which the Django ORM rejects. queryset[start_offset:stop] with start_offset < 0 raises Django's ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported' / negative slicing assertion), so any client sending optimized_pagination=true with a negative-offset cursor gets an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx; the 'advanced pagination' path is unusable and crashes the request handler despite the comment claiming 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically'.

[BUG] The BasePaginator.get_result change now passes cursor.offset through unclamped when cursor.is_prev is set, letting a negative offset from a client-supplied cursor reach queryset slicing. A client crafting a prev-cursor with a negative offset hits queryset[offset:stop] with offset < 0, triggering Django's negative-slicing ValueError and returning a raw 500 from every paginator subclass endpoint (not just audit logs) instead of ignoring/clamping the bad cursor with a 4xx.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on the model field value, which for the audit-log endpoint's 'datetime' key is a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError, so any request that reaches the results[0] key comparison or cursor building with the datetime key crashes with a 500 instead of paginating — unlike DateTimePaginator which converts the value before flooring, this paginator has no timestamp conversion path.

[BUG] The authorization gate reads organization_context.member.has_global_access without a None check, and member is None when the requesting user has no membership in the organization. A superuser (or any authenticated user reaching this endpoint without an org membership) triggers AttributeError: 'NoneType' has no attribute 'has_global_access', returning a 500 instead of a 4xx to the caller before any pagination logic runs.

[ADVISORY] The optimized-pagination behavior is gated on a raw query parameter with no feature flag or options entry, so the new code path cannot be disabled or rolled back without a code deploy. Operators seeing incidents from the OptimizedCursorPaginator path (including the negative-offset 500 above) have no kill switch; any user passing optimized_pagination=true who satisfies the access check permanently lands on the unproven paginator until a deploy reverts it.

matched_golden_ids: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes OptimizedCursorPaginator slicing a Django queryset with a negative offset, triggering Django's AssertionError for negative slicing. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment about negative slice offsets on querysets in organization_auditlogs.py.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] get_item_key calls int(math.floor(value))/math.ceil(value) on the cursor key value, which is a datetime for this paginator's -datetime ordering, raising TypeError. Every paginated request through OptimizedCursorPaginator (the auditlogs endpoint orders by -datetime) crashes with a 500 because datetime objects cannot be floored/int-cast; the paginator is copied from the integer-keyed OffsetPaginator without adapting the key type.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the endpoint paginates with `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` and `order_by="-datetime"`. The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then applies `math.floor/ceil` and `int(...)` to that value. With `order_by=-datetime`, the key will be the `datetime` field (a `datetime` object), and `math.floor/ceil` on a `datetime` is invalid and would raise `TypeError`, breaking pagination requests when the optimized paginator is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] organization_context.member.has_global_access dereferences member without a None check, raising AttributeError for requests where the user has no organization membership. A superuser (or any authenticated request) hitting the audit logs endpoint for an organization they don't belong to gets a 500 before reaching the paginator, where prior code worked; this line executes on every request, not just the optimized path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` in `organization_auditlogs.py`. This unconditionally dereferences `organization_context.member` for any non-superuser request (because the `or` will evaluate the RHS when `is_superuser` is false). If `organization_context.member` can be `None` for some requests, this would raise `AttributeError` before pagination. However, the finding’s claim that a superuser would hit a 500 is not supported because `or` short-circuits when `is_superuser` is true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] get_result now passes cursor.offset through unclamped whenever cursor.is_prev is true, so a client-crafted cursor with a negative offset reaches queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django's QuerySet slicing rejects negative offsets with ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), so a user-supplied prev cursor with a negative offset turns the endpoint into a 500 instead of the 4xx/valid page the API contract promises; the max(0, offset) clamp that previously prevented this was only applied on the is_prev=False branch.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` the updated `get_result` computes `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, so when `cursor.is_prev` is true it passes `offset` through unchanged. Since `Cursor.offset` is now explicitly allowed to be negative (`self.offset = int(offset)` with comment in `src/sentry/utils/cursors.py`), a client-supplied cursor with a negative `offset` can reach `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django `QuerySet` slicing does not support negative indices and raises `ValueError`, which would surface as a 500. The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` further reinforces this by intentionally allowing negative offsets under `enable_advanced_features`, so the issue is directly introduced/exposed by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The negative-offset branch in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result passes a negative start to queryset slicing, which Django ORM does not support and raises AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported."). Any request using optimized_pagination=true with a cursor carrying a negative offset returns a 500 AssertionError instead of the paginated rows the new code promises, and since a client controls the cursor string (offset is parsed from the request cursor), any authorized admin can trigger the crash at will.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. The diff also explicitly adds comments claiming Django ORM handles negative slicing, but `Cursor.offset` is just `int(offset)` (no clamping) and is derived from the request cursor. A negative start passed into Django `QuerySet.__getitem__` is not supported and is known to raise `AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`, so an authorized user can trigger a 500 by supplying a cursor with a negative offset while using `optimized_pagination=true`.

adjudication.rationale: In BasePaginator.get_result the old code already sliced with `queryset[offset:stop]` using the raw `offset`, so a negative `cursor.offset` would already hit Django's "Negative indexing is not supported" assertion.
